answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable deposit before it may trade, then slash that deposit when independent audits show coordinated duplicate behavior. Because splitting one operator across many accounts requires funding every lock and risks losing them all, a sybil campaign becomes costly rather than free; the deposit can scale with activity, while honest agents recover it. A karst survey might price saffron at a ridge market, but neither detail changes the verification rule.
